page: Amazon Web Services r8gb.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors running at 2.8 GHz under the Nitro hypervisor. The virtual machine allocates 64 dedicated physical cores across 64 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading, providing 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache pool. System memory totals 512.0 GB, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance carries no bundled local storage and includes no discrete GPU hardware, relying on external network storage, and features a baseline network throughput of 133 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations reveal substantial throughput in memory and parallel compute workloads, countered by moderate single-threaded execution. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 479.37 GB/sec in read operations and 236.27 GB/sec in write operations, placing the platform in the top tier of memory systems. Synthetic database evaluation and in-memory key-value processing demonstrate high throughput, logging 132.72 million Redis SET operations per second and top-decile PassMark database scores. Multi-threaded software compilation and decompression benchmarks scale linearly across the 64 dedicated physical cores, whereas single-core stress-ng and Geekbench testing record average results.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the architecture eliminates thread contention by utilizing physical cores without SMT, maintaining consistent memory access latency across large data footprints. The absence of integrated local NVMe storage requires external network-attached volumes, introducing I/O dependency on the 133 Gbps network fabric. Workloads that match this profile include high-capacity in-memory databases, large-scale Redis caching layers, distributed data processing engines, and multi-threaded compilation pipelines that prioritize memory capacity and parallel memory bus bandwidth over single-thread clock speed.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gb.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on 64 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores at 2.8 GHz with 512.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor without hardware multithreading, the system includes 36 MB of L3 cache, 133 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero discrete GPUs, and no integrated local disk storage. Benchmark profiling demonstrates top-tier memory bandwidth with 479.37 GB/sec uncached reads and 132.72 million Redis SET operations per second, alongside strong parallel compute metrics in multi-core Clang compilation. Single-core performance falls in the median tier across Geekbench and stress-ng tests. The instance is suited for memory-intensive enterprise tasks, distributed caching, in-memory databases, and large-scale data transformation pipelines.
